# Procurement and Vendor Management Stage Contracts

One entry per desk in the Procurement Vendor Management Command Desk suite. Use these when running the suite as a continuous lifecycle, so a desk can carry the work into the next stage instead of telling the user to invoke another skill.

## Stage order

```text
procurement-policy-desk
  -> intake-triage-desk
  -> vendor-risk-tiering-desk
  -> category-strategy-desk
  -> requirements-specification-desk
  -> supplier-discovery-desk
  -> sourcing-event-desk
  -> bid-evaluation-desk
  -> security-privacy-review-desk
  -> supplier-integrity-screening-desk
  -> pricing-negotiation-desk
  -> contract-execution-routing-desk
  -> vendor-onboarding-provisioning-desk
  -> supplier-performance-sla-desk
  -> supplier-relationship-governance-desk
  -> spend-analysis-desk
  -> renewal-consolidation-desk
  -> vendor-offboarding-desk
```

The order is a dependency chain, not a mandatory itinerary. Most requests run a subsequence and enter partway: a renewal notice that just surfaced enters at `renewal-consolidation-desk` and pushes backward into performance and pricing, a security questionnaire that arrived from a reviewer enters at `security-privacy-review-desk`, a supplier that missed its availability commitment enters at `supplier-performance-sla-desk`, a cost reduction target enters at `spend-analysis-desk` and pushes forward into consolidation and renegotiation, a tool a team already signed for enters at `intake-triage-desk` as a policy exception, and a supplier being replaced enters at `vendor-offboarding-desk` and runs a new sourcing cycle alongside the exit. Never run a stage ahead of the packet state it consumes, and record every skip with its reason.

`vendor-risk-tiering-desk` sits early because the tier is a property of the use case rather than of the supplier: it is determined by the data, the criticality, and the integration depth the business need implies, and it sets the diligence scope and the lead time that the sourcing timeline has to accommodate. Tiering after a supplier is chosen produces a timeline that discovers a twelve-week review requirement in week eleven.

The three diligence desks operate on separate evidence with separate reviewers and fan out, then converge before `pricing-negotiation-desk`, because an unremediated finding is a commercial position before signature and an issue log entry after it.

Each entry states the hard halt specific to that stage. The default posture everywhere else is to proceed with the assumption labeled inline against the supplier, contract, requirement, or spend line it affects, per `references/halt-taxonomy.md`.

## Contracts

### procurement-policy-desk
Requires: the procurement policy in force and its approval history, the delegation of authority matrix and the resolutions behind it, competitive thresholds and the sourcing method each band requires, the sole source conditions and who may invoke them, the buying channels available and what the policy intends for each, mandatory contract positions covering data protection, insurance minimums, audit rights, and liability floors, the exception history including who granted each and whether it expired, prior audit or control findings against the purchasing process.
Owns: the policy position that answers the request in front of it with the specific provision quoted rather than paraphrased, the threshold determination naming which sourcing method this value and this risk tier require, the buying channel decision covering catalog, purchase order, card, and existing agreement, the authority determination naming the approver and the provision that sets the level, the exception assessment stating what is being asked for, what control it removes, who can grant it, and for how long, the policy gaps where the situation is real and the policy simply does not address it, the split-purchase test where a set of requests appears sized to sit below a threshold, and the practices operating outside the policy, recorded as unauthorized practice rather than normalized because a business unit has done it that way for two years.
Hands to: `intake-triage-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Changing a threshold, adding a buying channel, or granting a standing exception removes a control from every future purchase, not just this one, and the person who owns the policy owns that consequence. This desk states what the policy requires and prepares the exception request; it does not decide that the policy should have said something else.

### intake-triage-desk
Requires: the intake request with the stated need and the requester, the business sponsor and the budget line, the estimated value stated as both annual and total contract value, the data and systems the solution would touch, the current contract portfolio and the tools already licensed, the category taxonomy, the spend history for the requester's cost center, the timeline claimed and what creates it, whether anything has already been said to a supplier or already signed.
Owns: the triaged request with a classified need expressed as a capability rather than as the product name the requester arrived with, the duplicate and overlap check against existing agreements naming the contracts that already cover part or all of it, the value assessment converting a monthly figure into total contract value including renewal terms so a commitment is not approved against its first invoice, the urgency test separating a contract that expires from a date somebody selected, the routing decision naming the sourcing method, the risk path, and the lead time each requires, the intake completeness record naming what the requester has not supplied and what it blocks, the existing-agreement route where the need is already covered and the correct answer is to use what the company has, and the requests that arrived already committed, recorded as a policy exception with the commitment already made rather than processed as though the decision were still open.
Hands to: `vendor-risk-tiering-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Routing a request into a channel that skips competition, skips diligence, or sits below a threshold it does not actually sit below is granting an exception, and this desk exists to identify when one is needed. An emergency designation is the most common form: it removes competition and compresses review, it is invoked by the person who is late, and it is authorized by someone accountable for the consequence rather than by the calendar.

### vendor-risk-tiering-desk
Requires: the business need with the data the solution would process and whose data it is, the systems and networks the supplier would reach, the criticality of the process it supports and what stops if the supplier stops, the integration model including identity federation, production access, and code execution, the regulatory regimes the engagement pulls in, the tiering criteria the program uses, the diligence requirements and actual lead times each tier triggers, prior assessments of the same supplier and what they covered, any known fourth-party dependencies.
Owns: the tier determination with the criteria that produced it stated line by line, the data classification naming the categories, the volume, and whether it is the company's own data or customer data held on trust, the criticality assessment naming what breaks, for whom, and how quickly, the integration depth assessment covering access, identity, and whether the supplier can execute code or reach production, the regulatory scope the engagement creates, the fourth-party exposure where the supplier's own critical dependencies are known, the diligence scope the tier obliges with the realistic lead time for each item so the sourcing timeline is built against it, the reassessment triggers that would change the tier later, and the tier inputs the request has not established, recorded as unassessed with the tier held at the level the unknown data would imply rather than at the level the timeline would prefer.
Hands to: `category-strategy-desk`, and directly to `security-privacy-review-desk` where the tier makes diligence the critical path.
Hard halt: security or privacy. A tier set below what the data classification and the access model support removes the review that the data required, and the tier is the only mechanism standing between customer data and a supplier nobody examined. Tier pressure is always downward and always arrives with a deadline attached. Where the evidence supports a higher tier than the timeline can absorb, that is a scheduling problem for the sponsor rather than a tiering judgment.

### category-strategy-desk
Requires: the spend baseline for the category from the payables ledger rather than from contract values, the supplier list with what each actually delivers, the contract portfolio with terms and end dates, the supply market structure including concentration and realistic alternatives, internal demand across business units and how it differs, switching costs and integration dependencies, the build, extend, or buy position where an internal capability exists, prior sourcing exercises in this category and what they achieved.
Owns: the category definition with an explicit boundary, since the argument about category strategy is usually an argument about what is in the category, the spend baseline reconciled to the ledger with the population stated, the supplier map showing who delivers what and where the same capability is bought twice, the supply market assessment covering concentration, alternatives, and the direction of pricing power, the sourcing approach per subcategory with the reasoning, the demand aggregation opportunity where business units buy the same thing separately, the build, extend, or buy position with the internal capability and its cost assessed rather than dismissed, the term alignment plan so contracts reach a common renewal point and the category can be sourced as one event, the sequencing that reflects when each contract can actually be moved, and the savings potential expressed as a range with its basis, never as a target back-solved from a number somebody was given.
Hands to: `requirements-specification-desk`.
Hard halt: source conflict. The payables ledger, the contract repository, and the business units disagree about what is actually in the category and what is actually being spent, which happens routinely because suppliers are recorded under brands in one system and legal entities in another, resellers sit between the company and the vendor, and a meaningful share of the category was never routed through procurement. A strategy built on the wrong population consolidates the wrong suppliers and reports savings against spend that was never there.

### requirements-specification-desk
Requires: the business outcome and how success would be recognized, the current-state process and its actual pain points rather than the feature list a demonstration produced, the users and their workflows, technical and integration constraints, the security and privacy requirements the risk tier obliges, accessibility conformance obligations, service level needs derived from what the business actually depends on, data residency and retention constraints, the exit requirements the company will need years from now, the evaluation criteria and weights the sourcing method requires.
Owns: the requirement set separated into mandatory and desirable with the consequence of each mandatory item stated, since every mandatory requirement removes bidders and some of them remove all but the incumbent, requirements expressed as capability and outcome rather than as one product's feature names, the statement of work with deliverables, acceptance criteria, and who does what, the service levels the business actually needs with the measurement method and the remedy attached to each, security, privacy, and accessibility requirements carried in from the tier and stated as contractable obligations rather than aspirations, the exit requirements covering data return format, retrieval window, and deletion obligation, written now because at termination the company has no leverage to add them, the common assumptions every bidder will price against including volume, term, and scope, the evaluation criteria with weights and scoring scales fixed before anything is issued, and the requirements no stakeholder would own, recorded as unowned rather than inferred from the product a sponsor already wants.
Hands to: `supplier-discovery-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. A requirement set is about to go to the market carrying mandatory items that encode one supplier's product rather than a business need, or evaluation criteria that were written after a preferred supplier was already identified. Requirements cannot be quietly changed after issue without restarting the process or treating bidders unequally, the specification is the most durable artifact of the whole exercise because the contract inherits it, and a specification written around an incumbent produces a competitive process with one possible outcome and a paper trail that says so.

### supplier-discovery-desk
Requires: the requirement set and the category strategy, the incumbent position including what is already contracted and what it costs, the supply market structure, analyst and peer input where it exists, the company's own prior experience with candidate suppliers including any terminated relationships, reseller and channel structures that determine who the contracting entity would actually be, the fairness regime governing pre-market contact, geographic and regulatory constraints on who can be used.
Owns: the longlist with the legal contracting entity identified for each candidate rather than the brand, since resellers, regional subsidiaries, and acquired products change who the company is actually contracting with, the market structure view covering concentration, viability, and which suppliers are plausibly able to serve at this scale, the incumbent assessment stating switching cost, switching lead time, and what the incumbent knows about the company's position, the shortlist criteria applied to reach an invited list with the reason each candidate was excluded, the request for information where the market is unfamiliar enough that requirements would otherwise be written blind, the pre-market engagement record showing which suppliers were contacted, by whom, when, and what was said, the capability gaps where no supplier in the market meets a mandatory requirement, which is a requirements problem rather than a market problem, and the candidates whose viability or capability could not be established, listed as unassessed rather than filled in from their own materials.
Hands to: `sourcing-event-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Contacting the market is a communication to suppliers and it starts a sales process the company then has to manage. In a regulated or public procurement it does more: unequal pre-market engagement can disqualify the supplier that helped shape the requirement and can void the process, so who is contacted and what they are told is authorized and documented before it happens rather than reconstructed afterward.

### sourcing-event-desk
Requires: the requirement set and statement of work, the evaluation criteria and weights fixed and dated, the invited bidder list with contracting entities, the timeline with the question deadline and the submission deadline, the fairness regime and any mandated process, the contract template and the terms bidders are being asked to accept, the response format that makes bids comparable, the confidentiality regime protecting bid contents, the named point of contact through whom all communication runs.
Owns: the sourcing document with requirements, statement of work, response format, evaluation criteria and weights, timeline, and terms, issued as one coherent package rather than as a requirements list bidders answer in their own shape, the pricing template that forces a common structure so bids arrive comparable instead of being normalized after the fact, the single channel of communication with every question and its answer distributed to all bidders together, the addenda record where a clarification changes the requirement, with the submission deadline extended where the change is material, the late and non-conforming submission handling stated in advance and applied as stated, the confidentiality controls that keep one bidder's content away from the others and away from the incumbent, the terms exceptions process so bidders declare their positions during the bid rather than during the negotiation, the participation record including who declined and why, since a market that declines is telling the company something about its requirements, and the process deviations that occurred, recorded as deviations with what they affect rather than smoothed out of the record.
Hands to: `bid-evaluation-desk`.
Hard halt: production or destructive. Issuing the document and answering a bidder question are acts against the market that cannot be recalled. An answer given to one bidder and not the others is unequal treatment that taints the process, a requirement corrected after submissions have arrived either restarts the exercise or advantages whoever already knew, and in a regulated procurement either one is a ground for challenge that survives the award.

### bid-evaluation-desk
Requires: the submitted bids with everything each supplier provided, the evaluation criteria and weights as fixed and dated before issue, the evaluator panel and their independence from the outcome, the common assumptions bids were priced against, the pricing templates as returned, exceptions each bidder took to terms and service levels, demonstration and proof of concept results, reference contacts and what is to be asked, the risk tier and any diligence findings already available.
Owns: independent scores per evaluator against the published criteria with the evidence in the response cited for each score, recorded before evaluators confer, the consensus record showing where evaluators diverged, what resolved it, and who was present, the normalized total cost comparison restated onto a common term, scope, and volume with every normalization stated, since the normalization is the analysis and the headline price rarely survives it, the criteria a bid did not address, left unscored and reported as unanswered rather than assigned a middle score to keep the arithmetic tidy, the terms exception comparison showing what each bidder would actually sign, the reference findings with who was spoken to, at which organization, and what was asked, the demonstration findings recording what was observed rather than what was presented, the award recommendation with the scoring outcome and the commercial position stated separately so a reader can see which one decided it, the debrief position prepared for each unsuccessful bidder, and any change to criteria or weights with its date and whether bids were visible at the time, recorded permanently.
Hands to: `security-privacy-review-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. An award recommendation would leave the evaluation team without the scoring evidence behind it, or scores would be adjusted after bids became visible. This is the defining integrity failure of the profession: the decision is made first and the scorecard is filled in to support it, and it is detectable precisely because the weights or the scores moved after the bids were open. A losing bidder with a relationship inside the company will ask how the decision was reached, a regulated process gives them a formal route to ask, and the answer is whatever the record shows.

### security-privacy-review-desk
Requires: the risk tier and the diligence scope it obliges, the data classification and processing description including data flows and locations, the supplier's attestation reports with their full scope, period, and exception sections, penetration test evidence, the completed security questionnaire, the subprocessor list and its notification terms, the transfer mechanism for any cross-border flow, the company's own security and privacy requirements, the named reviewers in the security and privacy functions, the deadline the sourcing timeline assumes.
Owns: the review coordination record naming who is reviewing what, what evidence was requested, what arrived, and what is outstanding with a date, the attestation analysis stating the report type and edition, the services actually in scope, the period covered, and the exceptions and qualifications the report contains, since the exceptions section carries the information and the cover page carries the reassurance, the gap between the service being purchased and the service the report covers, which is the most common defect in supplier security evidence and is invisible unless someone reads the scope statement, the questionnaire review treating answers as assertions to be corroborated rather than as findings, the processing role determination and the data protection terms it requires, the subprocessor position with locations and the objection rights the agreement grants, the transfer mechanism relied on, the findings register with severity, the supplier's response, the compensating control where one exists, a named owner, and a due date, the conditions attached to any conditional approval, each with an owner and a date because a condition with neither is an unconditional approval wearing a caveat, the terms the review requires the contract to carry so they enter the negotiation rather than the issue log, and the claims the supplier makes that no document supports, recorded as vendor-claimed and never promoted by repetition.
Hands to: `supplier-integrity-screening-desk`.
Hard halt: security or privacy. Continuing would treat a supplier as reviewed when the evidence for the service being bought does not exist, would move personal or customer data to a processor whose terms and subprocessors are unestablished, or would let an approval condition pass into the contract with no owner and no date. This desk coordinates the review and does not perform it, and it never substitutes its own judgment for a reviewer who has not responded. Where the review cannot complete inside the timeline, the timeline is the thing that moves.

### supplier-integrity-screening-desk
Requires: the legal contracting entity with its registration details and jurisdiction, ownership and control information including recent changes of control, the screening lists the company's policy requires and a provider to run them against, debarment and exclusion sources where public sector work is involved, financial information appropriate to the commitment length and value, insurance requirements from the policy and the certificates the supplier provides, anti-bribery and conflict of interest declarations, labor and sustainability obligations the company carries into its own reporting, the requirements each of these has to satisfy.
Owns: the entity verification confirming the company is screening and contracting with the same legal person, including where a reseller or a regional subsidiary sits between the company and the product, the ownership and control picture to the depth the policy requires, screening results naming the lists checked, the provider, the date, and the outcome, since a screening result is true as of the moment it ran and nothing else, the debarment and exclusion check, the conflict of interest review covering declared relationships between the supplier and anyone in the decision, which is the finding people are least comfortable raising and most likely to leave out, the anti-bribery assessment where intermediaries, agents, or public officials are involved, the financial viability assessment matched to the commitment being made, since a three-year critical dependency on a supplier with a going concern question is a different decision from a one-year subscription, the insurance verification checking coverage type, limit, expiry, and whether the certificate names the company where the contract requires it, the labor and sustainability position where the company has to report on its supply chain, and the checks that could not be completed, reported as not performed with the reason rather than presented as clear.
Hands to: `pricing-negotiation-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. A screening match, a debarment, an undeclared conflict of interest, or an unresolved beneficial ownership question is cleared by legal and compliance and never inside procurement. These findings carry criminal and regulatory exposure rather than commercial risk, the pressure to interpret a partial name match as a false positive is highest exactly when the deal is urgent, and clearing one here is the control failing at the only moment it was designed to work.

### pricing-negotiation-desk
Requires: the evaluated bids with their normalized totals, the diligence findings and the terms the reviews require, the should-cost inputs and any benchmarks with their sources and dates, the incumbent's current pricing and the actual switching cost, the supplier's position including their fiscal calendar and what the company knows about their motivation, the company's requirements ranked by what it would actually give up, the walk-away position and the realistic alternative if this supplier is declined, the authority levels the value engages, the leverage window and what closes when.
Owns: the should-cost model with its method and inputs stated, the benchmark set where genuine comparables exist, each with its source, date, and scope, the total cost position across the full horizon including implementation, integration, training, internal effort, and exit, the term structure position covering initial term, renewal mechanics, ramp, uplift caps, and price protection, since the renewal terms agreed today decide the negotiation three years from now and cost nothing to fix while the deal is still open, the commitment mechanics covering minimums, true-up and true-down rights, overage rates, and what happens to unused entitlement, the negotiation plan with objectives ranked, tradeables identified, and a concession sequence where each concession is exchanged rather than given, the walk-away position and the credible alternative behind it, since a walk-away with nothing behind it is a bluff the supplier has already priced, the unremediated diligence findings converted into contract terms while leverage still exists, the leverage position stating what is open, what closes when, and what the company has already told the supplier, and the price positions with no comparable behind them, recorded as no comparable found rather than expressed as a market rate.
Hands to: `contract-execution-routing-desk`.
Hard halt: production or destructive. A price, a target, a budget figure, a deadline, or an intention that reaches the supplier cannot be withdrawn, and the supplier reprices to whatever it heard. The most expensive sentence in this domain is a sponsor telling a supplier they have won before the terms are agreed, because every concession still available before that moment is gone after it and nothing the negotiator does afterward recovers it. This desk prepares the position, the model, and the script; the person with authority delivers it.

### contract-execution-routing-desk
Requires: the agreed commercial position, the terms the diligence reviews require, the contract template and whose paper the agreement will sit on, the document set with every exhibit, the legal reviewer and the redlines already exchanged, the approval chain the value and risk tier require with the provision that sets each level, the signature authority, the purchase order requirement for this channel, the effective date the business needs and what depends on it.
Owns: the contract request package giving legal the commercial terms, the requirements, the diligence findings, the service levels, and the risk tier in one place rather than as a forwarded thread, the document set inventory with every exhibit and its version, the order of precedence position or the explicit record that the documents lack one, which is a defect worth fixing before signature and impossible to fix after, the open positions with the company position, the supplier position, and the named risk owner for each, the approval routing with each role, the authority basis, and the state, assembled in the sequence the policy requires so an approver is not asked to ratify a decision already communicated, the signature routing to the person the authority matrix actually names rather than the person who is available, the execution record with the signed document, its location, and its effective date, the date extraction taken from the executed document covering effective date, initial term end, renewal type, notice window, and the computed notice deadline with a named owner, the obligation register listing what each party owes with owners and dates on the company's side, and the terms that were conceded, recorded as accepted risk with the owner who accepted them rather than absorbed into the file.
Hands to: `vendor-onboarding-provisioning-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Signature commits the company for the full term at the agreed price, and it is the last reversible moment in the sequence. The authority matrix names who may sign at this value, that person is the one who signs, and an approval chain compressed because the effective date is tomorrow is the chain not operating. Countersigning a supplier's order form is signing, regardless of how routine the document looks.

### vendor-onboarding-provisioning-desk
Requires: the executed agreement with its commercial and security terms, the vendor master requirements including tax and compliance forms, the banking details and the verification method the policy requires, the access the supplier needs and the approval behind each grant, the security configuration the review obliges covering identity federation, provisioning, logging, retention, and administrative roles, the invoicing and purchase order setup, the named internal owner, the adoption plan and the usage the business case assumed.
Owns: the vendor master record request with the legal entity, tax forms, and compliance documentation, the bank detail verification performed against a channel the requester did not supply and recorded with the named person who performed it and how, the access provisioning record listing each system, the level granted, who approved it, and the review that authorized it, the security configuration as actually implemented rather than as the contract requires, including identity federation, automated provisioning and deprovisioning, log delivery, retention settings, administrative role assignment, and network restrictions, since a security review that produced requirements nobody configured has protected nothing, the invoicing setup with the billing contact, the purchase order requirement, and the coding that will let spend be attributed later, the named internal owner recorded against the supplier, because a supplier with no owner is the one nobody renegotiates and the one that auto-renews, the obligation handoff giving the owner the dates, the service levels, and the conditions they now carry, the adoption plan against the usage the business case assumed so consumption can be measured against it, and the onboarding steps that were skipped to meet a go-live date, recorded as open with what each one leaves exposed.
Hands to: `supplier-performance-sla-desk`.
Hard halt: security or privacy. Two acts here are irreversible in the way that matters. A bank detail added or changed on an unverified instruction sends money to whoever asked, and this is the single most productive fraud pattern aimed at any company, arriving as an urgent request from a familiar name with an approval chain conveniently shortened. Granting a supplier access to systems or data before the review governing that access has closed turns a reviewable decision into an exposure nobody chose, and access granted for a go-live is rarely revisited.

### supplier-performance-sla-desk
Requires: the contracted service levels with their definitions, exclusions, and remedies, the measurement source and whose telemetry decides, the performance data for the period, incident history with impact and the supplier's root cause statements, support ticket volumes and resolution times, the scorecard dimensions the relationship's tier justifies, the consumption data against purchased entitlement, the business case outcomes and whether they arrived, escalation history and what came of it.
Owns: the scorecard covering delivery, quality, responsiveness, commercial behavior, and risk posture, with the measurement source named for each dimension, the service level results comparing the commitment to the measured outcome, with the definition's exclusions read rather than assumed, since scheduled maintenance, degraded performance, and single-region outages frequently sit outside the calculation and the difference decides whether a breach occurred, the credit position showing credits earned, claimed, and received, since credits are almost never applied automatically and a credit nobody claimed is a discount the company chose not to take, the distinction between contractual compliance and business outcome, because a supplier can meet every commitment while the thing the company bought does not work, the incident record with impact and the supplier's account of cause, the consumption against entitlement position with the true-up or reduction it implies, the improvement plan with milestones and a consequence attached where performance is below the bar, the escalation path invoked according to the contract's own remedies rather than a generic ladder, and the dimensions with no measurement behind them, reported as unmeasured rather than scored on impression.
Hands to: `supplier-relationship-governance-desk`.
Hard halt: source conflict. The supplier's reported performance and the company's own telemetry disagree about whether a commitment was met, which is routine because the definitions differ, the exclusions differ, and the supplier is measuring itself. Asserting a breach on the wrong measurement forfeits the claim and damages a relationship the company may not be able to leave; accepting the supplier's figure without reading the definition means no commitment is ever measured. Record both readings with their sources and the definition each used.

### supplier-relationship-governance-desk
Requires: the supplier portfolio with values, tiers, and criticality, performance history and scorecard trends, the concentration position across categories, business units, and legal entities, dependency and substitutability analysis, switching cost and realistic switching lead time, the contract terms that govern exit and transition, the supplier's own strategic direction including ownership changes and product end-of-life notices, the governance cadence in place and who attends, escalation and dispute history.
Owns: the portfolio segmentation classifying suppliers by value and by criticality with the basis stated, since spend and importance diverge sharply and the cheapest supplier in the portfolio is frequently the one that can stop the business, the concentration view computed across entities and business units, where a supplier that looks minor in each unit turns out to be critical to the company, the dependency assessment naming what the company cannot do without them, the substitutability position with realistic alternatives and what moving would actually take, the distinction between a single source position the company chose and a sole source position the market imposed, which need opposite responses, the exit readiness assessment stating whether an exit could be executed today and naming exactly what is missing, the governance cadence matched to tier and value with the agenda, the attendees, and decisions recorded with owners, the relationship risks including the supplier's own financial trajectory, acquisition exposure, and product direction, the joint roadmap where the relationship justifies one, and the continuity claims the company cannot evidence, stated as untested rather than asserted.
Hands to: `spend-analysis-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. A continuity or exit readiness position is about to leave the company, into a customer security questionnaire, a regulator response, an audit, or a board risk report, without evidence behind it. An untested exit plan for a critical supplier is an assumption written in the format of a control, and it is relied on by readers who have no way to tell the difference. The company inherits its suppliers' claims into its own attestations, and it answers for them.

### spend-analysis-desk
Requires: the payables ledger for the period with supplier, amount, cost center, and coding, the contract portfolio with values and terms, the purchase order data and the buying channels used, the category taxonomy and the supplier-to-entity mapping, the vendor master with parent and subsidiary relationships, card and expense data where purchases route around the requisition process, prior savings claims and how finance treated them, budget lines the spend consumes.
Owns: the spend baseline built from what the company actually paid rather than from what it contracted for, with the population and the period stated, the supplier consolidation across brands, resellers, subsidiaries, and misspelled vendor master entries, without which the same supplier appears four times and the concentration disappears, the category view with the taxonomy applied and the uncategorized remainder reported at its full amount, the contract coverage position separating spend under an agreement from spend with nothing behind it, the off-contract and off-channel spend with the buying unit identified where the data allows, the tail analysis with its supplier count and aggregate value, since the tail is where the effort-to-value ratio is worst and where the risk is entirely unreviewed, the price variance where the same item or service is bought at different prices across the company, the fragmentation view naming where several suppliers deliver one capability, the savings realization comparing what was negotiated to what the ledger shows, with realized saving and avoided cost separated and the budget line named where finance recognized it, and the spend that cannot be attributed, reported as unattributed at its full amount rather than distributed across categories on a proportional assumption.
Hands to: `renewal-consolidation-desk`.
Hard halt: connector unreachable. The payables ledger cannot be read and the analysis would be assembled from the contract repository, purchase orders, or supplier statements instead. Each of those describes intention rather than payment, and all three systematically omit exactly the off-contract and card spend the analysis exists to find, so the resulting picture is cleanest where the problem is worst. A ledger that is merely incomplete for a period is a stated gap; a ledger that cannot be reached is this halt.

### renewal-consolidation-desk
Requires: the executed agreements with their term, renewal type, notice window, and the clause each comes from, the renewal calendar across the portfolio, current pricing and the uplift the renewal terms permit, consumption against entitlement, performance history and open issues, the business need as it stands now rather than as it stood at signature, alternatives and their switching cost, overlapping agreements that could consolidate, the decision owner for each contract.
Owns: the renewal calendar built from executed documents with the notice deadline computed from the clause and the date basis it counts from, and the source of every date stated, since a repository field is a transcription and the notice window is the field that gets transcribed wrong, the decision window naming the date by which each decision has to be made to keep options open, which is always earlier than the renewal date and is the date that actually matters, the renewal position per contract covering price, uplift exposure, consumption against entitlement, performance, and whether the need still exists, the consolidation candidates with combined value, overlapping scope, and the term alignment that makes or blocks a consolidation, the rationalization case where several tools deliver one capability, with the migration cost and the internal disruption stated rather than assumed away, the portfolio view clustering renewals by supplier and by quarter, because three agreements with one supplier are one negotiation with three deadlines and treating them separately gives the supplier three chances and the company none, the renegotiation position built while notice is still available, the notice documents prepared to the form and method the clause requires, and the contracts whose executed document could not be located, reported as dates unestablished with the retrieval action, never with a date inferred from a calendar entry or a repository field.
Hands to: `vendor-offboarding-desk` where the decision is to exit, and back into `pricing-negotiation-desk` where it is to renegotiate.
Hard halt: approval. Both directions commit the company. Serving notice starts a clock against the supplier and cannot be recalled; letting a term renew commits another full period at the contracted uplift and is performed by nobody, which is what makes it the most common expensive mistake in the function. Where an executed document cannot be reached and a notice window is open, escalate immediately rather than working the queue in order, because that halt costs money every day it stands and it converts into an unrecoverable outcome on a known date.

### vendor-offboarding-desk
Requires: the executed agreement with its termination, transition assistance, data return, and deletion clauses, the termination basis and the notice the clause requires, the data the supplier holds and where it lives, the systems the supplier can reach and the accounts held by its personnel, the replacement plan and the overlap period, outstanding invoices, credits, and unused prepayment, the records the company has to retain, the knowledge that exists only inside the supplier relationship, the internal owner and the affected users.
Owns: the termination package with the basis, the clause relied on, and the notice prepared in the form and by the method the contract requires, since a notice sent by an unspecified method to an unspecified address is contested at exactly the moment it matters, the transition plan sequencing the replacement with a realistic overlap, the data return specification covering scope, format, and the retrieval window the contract actually grants, executed while the agreement is still in force, the deletion obligation with the certification the contract requires and a record of whether it arrived, the access deprovisioning record covering the supplier's access to company systems and the company's own accounts on the supplier's platform, each with a date and a named confirmer, the final settlement covering last invoices, credits owed, unused prepayment, and disputed amounts, the record retention position naming what the company keeps, where, and for how long after the relationship ends, the knowledge transfer where the supplier holds operational understanding nobody internal has, the residual dependency register naming anything still running on the supplier after the stated exit date, and the obligations that survive termination, listed with their duration rather than treated as ended because the relationship is.
Hands to: `procurement-vendor-management-command-desk` for the closure record, and into `spend-analysis-desk` so the exit is visible in the next baseline.
Hard halt: production or destructive. The exit sequence is externally constrained and getting it wrong destroys assets: data extraction has to complete while the contract is still in force and before the termination effective date, because retrieval is frequently disabled on that date and the transition assistance obligation ends with the term. Deprovisioning ahead of extraction removes the access the extraction needs. Final payment is the last leverage that exists to obtain a deletion certificate, and once it is released the supplier has no commercial reason to produce one. Prepare the sequence; the notice, the deprovisioning, and the final payment are each released by a named owner.

## Packet rule

Every stage updates `procurement_packet` as defined in `references/suite-workflow-contract.md` before handing off. Source facts, assumptions, approvals, open conditions, and unestablished dates accumulate across stages and are never dropped to keep an artifact short. An item removed from an open list is removed with its resolution and the date, because the same expiring insurance certificate, the same unowned approval condition, and the same supplier that keeps missing its response times resurface every cycle, and the useful record is what was decided last time and why.

Every carried fact keeps the date it was established. This is where the packet fails in this domain if it fails at all: an attestation, a screening result, an insurance certificate, a financial assessment, a price quote, and a subprocessor list are all facts with expiry dates, and a packet that carries the value without the date turns a fact that was true last year into a fact that is true now. A supplier reassessed on inherited evidence has not been reassessed. When a stage re-reads a carried supplier fact whose date has passed its validity, the correct entry is the stale value with its date and a re-request, not a refreshed value nobody obtained.
